data.body:
THE LAST UNMET CRITERION IS NOW SATISFIED — Gerrit 1190 MERGED.

The close gate refused on: "the three researched numbers ... are each either confirmed against the
target DC version or explicitly marked unverified". It was right — the shipped code stated all
three as plain facts. That criterion existed for a specific reason: the OSS research they came from
RETRACTED two of its other claims on a second pass, so an unlabelled number is exactly the
over-trust it was guarding against.

Change 1190 labels each at the point of use, in `retry.py`'s comment on `_RETRY_AFTER_JITTER` and
in the test module's docstring:
  * "Data Center only" — CONFIRMED. `/rest/api/2/serverInfo` reports `deploymentType != "Cloud"`,
    asserted live by `test_instance_is_a_server_deployment_at_the_pinned_version`.
  * "8.6+" — CONFIRMED SATISFIED, which is deliberately weaker than confirming the threshold. The
    harness runs 8.17.1 and that live test asserts `>= (8, 14)`, so the instance is comfortably
    above 8.6. That 8.6 is the exact version the limiter ARRIVED in is marked **UNVERIFIED** —
    documentation, not tested.
  * "off by default (admin-enabled)" — marked **UNVERIFIED**. Whether the limiter is enabled is an
    admin setting this suite never reads and the harness has never had switched on.
  * "Retry-After + up to 20% jitter" — marked **UNVERIFIED against a live limiter**. No test has
    observed a real 429 from a real token bucket, because the harness cannot produce one.

AND THE POINT THAT MAKES THIS SAFE RATHER THAN MERELY HONEST: none of the four is load-bearing.
The retry keys off the PRESENCE of a `Retry-After` header, never off any assumption about the
limiter's version or default. With no header the code behaves exactly as it did before this story,
so being wrong about any of them costs nothing at runtime. That is a property of the design, not a
disclaimer — and it is why the "static pacing policy is NOT implementable" constraint in the plan
led to header-driven retry in the first place.

Comment and docstring only; no behaviour change; the ten held-out tests still pass.
